5. OR gate output when all inputs are 0 — e) 0
AND gate: Y = A∙B — output 1 only when ALL inputs are 1. Symbol: D-shape with flat input side. Truth table: 00→0, 01→0, 10→0, 11→1. Example: two series switches lighting one lamp.
OR gate: Y = A+B — output 1 when ANY input is 1. Symbol: curved input side, pointed output. Truth table: 00→0, 01→1, 10→1, 11→1. Example: doorbell wired to two parallel push-buttons.
NOT gate: Y = A̅ — output is the inverse of the input. Symbol: triangle with inversion bubble. Truth table: 0→1, 1→0. Example: light that turns ON when a dark sensor reads 0.
